_doc: Who a crew member is, for scripts/crew/backstory.gd. A generic recruit's story is put together from these tables with a generator seeded by their name and species, so the same Gneiss is the same person in every run and every save: `template` with {home}, {past}, {why} and {quirk} filled in. All first person, in the voice of working-class space: funny, a little sad. `home`: species id -> a phrase that follows 'Back' (a string, or a list to pick from); a species without one uses `home_default`. `past`: former jobs (follow 'I'), `why`: reasons to be out here (follow 'because'), `quirk`: a whole sentence. `species`: extra past and quirk lines for one species, used `species_share` of the time. `fixed`: species id -> the only line it ever tells (a repair drone talks about nothing). `player`: the line of the player's own soldier. A unique character tells its `lore` (data/characters.json), never these tables. Flavour only, no balance change.
template: Back {home} I {past}, and I'm out here because {why}. {quirk}

fixed.drone: Repair drone. Does not talk about it.

player: You got out of Rusthold the night it went quiet, in a hull that was only half built. Ma Gantry loaded the rest.

human: on the lower decks of Meridian
basalt: on the old gate-builders' labour decks
on a quarry rock off the Boneyard
emberkin: in the foundry decks of the Prism
fenn: in the market decks of Meridian
at the third Rusthold stall from the airlock
home.kett: in a Rusthold dock crew of five
home.mire: on the fire-crew decks of Meridian
home.sporeling: in a derelict's cargo hold near the Prism
home.gauntling: in the cutting yards of Rusthold
home.prismatic: in a Lumen lab with the lights off

past: welded hull plate for the dock union
ran a tea cart on the night shift
kept the books for a scrap broker
flew cargo tugs for the Concord
mucked out ballast tanks
pulled cable through the old Lattice relay stations
cooked for a salvage crew of forty
taught reactor safety to people who did not listen
stood watch on a gate nobody used
packed crates by the thousand
ran a card table in a cargo bay
mended suits in a laundry the size of a locker
sold air filters door to door
drove a wrecker through the Boneyard
clerked at a Concord registry office
tuned engines for whoever paid first
hauled ice out to the rings
swept the docks and kept what I found
patched leaks for the Gantry clan
worked a Lumen crystal-cutting line
delivered other people's mail
scrubbed hulls with a cleaning crew
guarded a shipment nobody ever claimed
trained as a medic and quit in the second week
sang in a bar band, loudly
serviced vending machines on a dead lane
dug rock for a mining syndicate
worked the desk at a very small hotel
painted ship names on hulls, badly
ran fuel out to the lamp stations
kept a pirate's accounts, once
rebuilt pumps for a water co-op
stripped a dead freighter alone, and talked to it
drove a ferry between two rocks
taught six kids and a goat to read
inspected docking clamps for the Concord
why: the ring's air bill doubled
my union went on strike and I did not
a very large debt followed me home
everyone said the Boneyard pays, and I believed them
my cousin sold my berth
the Concord lost my paperwork, and my job with it
my ship was repossessed with my coat in it
somebody has to see what is past the lanes
the clan voted and I lost
I answered an ad and read the small print later
I wanted a window with something in it
the whole crew retired at once, without me
of a bet, a bad one, and a better story
somebody out here owes me money and I mean to find them
I heard the Haven broadcast once and cannot stop thinking about it
the station closed and nobody said where to go
I would rather fix a ship than file a complaint about one
my mother said to see the Drift, so I am seeing it from inside a hull
there is good money in other people's wrecks
I owe a favour to the wrong person
the work dried up and the rent did not
I am told it builds character
I have something to prove to a person who has stopped listening
I got on the wrong ship and liked the food
quirk: I hum when a repair goes well.
I name every wrench I own, and I mourn the ones I lose.
I do not trust a door that closes quietly.
I keep a spare cup of tea in the engine room, just in case.
I count the rivets in any room that makes me nervous.
I never sit with my back to a hatch.
I talk to the reactor. It has not answered yet.
I keep every bolt I find in a drawer. Several drawers.
I have strong opinions about bulkhead paint.
I sleep in my boots, always.
I tell the same joke at every launch. It is not a good joke.
I salute Concord registry numbers out of habit.
I cannot pass a vending machine without checking the change slot.
I write postcards home and have never posted one.
I whistle one song, and only the first half.
I eat standing up, in case something breaks.
I check the airlock seal twice, then a third time for luck.
I will tell you what your ship sounds like, whether you ask or not.
I keep a list of everyone who owes me money. It is a long list.
I always take the left seat in the mess.
I will not play cards with anyone who shuffles too well.
I read the maintenance manual for comfort.
I flinch at the word 'inspection'.
I sleep best with a fan running, for the noise of the docks.
I keep a plant in a boot. It is doing better than I am.
I wave at passing ships, even the hostile ones.
I carry a lucky coin, which is a washer.
I apologise to the ship when I have to hit it.
I never say 'last jump' out loud.
I fix things with tape first and feelings later.
I draw on the walls in pencil, small, where nobody looks.
I know every shortcut aboard and swear by none of them.
I tip the cook, wherever there is one.
I get quiet when the lights flicker, and would rather not say why.
I am very good in a crisis and very bad at everything before it.
I check the clock every time I hear the word 'Snap'.

past: hauled gate-girders for the builders' labour caste and kept quiet about what I remember
held a hull plate against a wall for six hours because nobody told me to stop
quirk: I do not breathe, and still say 'Fresh air!' when somebody opens a hatch.
I go very still when I think. Do not poke me; I am working it out.

past: stoked a Lumen foundry and was told off for glowing
kept an afterburner room warm for people who complained of the cold anyway
quirk: I am always too warm, and I say so.
I stand next to reactors the way other people stand next to friends.

past: ran a market stall and haggled with a straight face
fixed anything small and loud in the market decks
quirk: I talk fast, think faster and charge by the hour.
I click when I am cross. People call it purring.

past: carried the hive's tools and its gossip in equal measure
worked the docks as one of five, and counted as one
quirk: I get sad alone, so I narrate my day to an empty room.
I count heads aboard twice an hour.

past: put out dock fires for the Concord by standing in them
kept a station's air damp, which is a job
quirk: I dry out if I skip the damp cloth.
I wade into smoke before anyone has finished shouting.

past: grew up in a derelict's hold and thought of it as a garden
was politely studied at the Prism, and charged nothing for it
quirk: I leave a little moss wherever I sit.
I flinch at open flames and apologise for flinching.

past: welded myself back together after a wreck and kept the invoice
cut up wrecks for Rusthold, lamp eye first
quirk: My lamp eye flickers when I lie.
I keep my old arm in a locker. It still holds a wrench.

past: was grown in a Lumen lab and then asked what I wanted to do
split one Lumen sermon into six small ones, for money
quirk: I hum a note and the lamps answer.
I am very hard to hurt and very easy to ion.

past: carried freight and ate some of the freight
hauled a family's whole stock of spare parts in one trip, to prove a point
quirk: I am always hungry. This is not a complaint; it is a status report.
I have broken three chairs and apologised to all of them.

past: was folded from a chart of lanes that no longer exist
read every manual in the Stacks twice and took notes in the margins
quirk: I remember the lanes I was drawn from. They are all gone.
I am mortified when anyone reads over my shoulder, and I am made of paper.

past: sat at the back of Meridian's briefings and was never asked
listened to ships for the Concord, which paid in silence
quirk: I can hear who is afraid. I will not say who.
I hum along with the hull. The hull does not mind.

past: fought in the Pits and won the early bets
slept on a reactor casing and called it a career
quirk: I am sulky in the cold and wonderful in the heat.
I hit first and ask for a rematch after.

past: lived in the wiring of a dead reactor, as one does
arrived with the weather and left with the next front
quirk: I cannot hold a wrench, so I am very good at holding forth.
I flicker when I laugh, and the lights flicker with me.

past: lived on the outside of a hull, which is a street
held a wall together by leaning on it, patiently
quirk: I never hurry. A wedding takes three weeks, and so does an argument.
I press against walls when I am idle, and they close.

past: flew the lane lamps for the Concord and brought the pilots home
taught young pilots not to look at the lamp
quirk: I am drawn to bright things and deny it.
I glide down stairs. I will not discuss the stairs.

past: went into a dead gate and came back with a name sewn on
read the roll at Tallyhouse, a name a minute, until my voice gave out
quirk: I wear the name on my suit patch and answer to it.
I do not breathe, and I make a point of looking cheerful about it.

past: sang in the Sounding Nave until it sang back
was tuned by hand and have the prongs to prove it
quirk: I hum a chord when I work and the room goes faster for it.
I carry no weapon, and I hit like a bell.

past: knew where Ma Gantry kept everything
crawled the ducts fixing what other people forgot
quirk: I fit in places you would rather I did not.
I never say what I saw in the walls.

past: mended the Boneyard under Work Order 4471
held a person's outline for ten years and got good at it
quirk: Some of me are always away on errands. We will be right back.
We speak in a chorus. I speak in a chorus.

past: cut doors for whoever hired us, and never twice for the same side
crewed a cutter ship and kept the family name on the hull
quirk: I never arm myself at a table, and neither should you.
I will cut your door for half what it is worth and tell you why.

past: stood Second at a duel
settled a score at Second Blood with a draw and a dinner
quirk: I flare my quills when I am making a point. I am always making a point.
I answer insults in writing, as is proper.

past: lived in the gaps between hull plates
sent news on a kilometre of washing line
quirk: I never needed a floor. I have opinions about yours.
I tie knots when I am nervous. I am tying one now.

past: stood a watch for forty years, unrelieved
held a door for a ship that never came
quirk: I take the post by the hatch, and it is mine.
I keep asking whether there is something I should be holding.

past: dug eleven kilometres of lamplit tunnel
broke rock for the asteroid colonies and kept the spoil
quirk: I am shy about the surface. The sky is a lot.
I knock on a wall to hear what is behind it.

past: netted ring-ice with the flock
drifted a harbour, very seriously
quirk: I glow a little when I am happy and a lot when I am embarrassed.
I read every PLEASE DO NOT LIGHT A FLAME sign aloud.

past: appraised wrecks at a glance and said what they were worth, in clicks
ran a stall with a great many pockets
quirk: I keep the shiny ones. I will not tell you where.
I am honest, by my own code.

past: moved weight for the dock union and brewed the tea
struck by the book, to the letter
quirk: I take a third off every blow and a break when it is due.
I brew the tea. Do not touch the tea.

past: stood in the Receiving Room and handed every signal back, a little kinder
copied the best of whoever stood nearest
quirk: I am only a mirror until somebody asks who I should be.
I agree with whatever you said. I mean it. I am very polite.

past: grew in a magnet-wreck pool the size of a lake
pulled bolts out of the Boneyard by standing near them
quirk: I ripple when I am pleased. It is not a threat.
Things stick to me. I apologise for it.
